about_text.value: The Mediator was found erased from the ledger of power, a victim of institutional deadlock that forces uneasy settlements while influence remains a conserved pool. The Counter Archivist investigates why the system consumed its own broker. Across this age, the civilizational wager is refracted through memory, scarcity, and ambition; every institutional move recasts trust, resentment, and the archive of prior catastrophes. As evidence leaks and paradox-proof memory fails, the detective must decide whether to cancel quiet influence with proof or let the deadlock settle into a new equilibrium. The truth lies not in who pulled the trigger, but in what was sacrificed for the balance of power.

characters.name: The Counter Archivist
characters.description: A patient anti-institution that keeps a mirror-ledger of power: it cancels quiet influence with evidence, leaks, and paradox-proof memory.

characters.name: The Mediator
characters.description: A broker of uneasy settlements who tracks public sentiment and timing windows.

characters.name: The New Men
characters.description: The New Men is pulled into the murder inquiry by motive, alibi, or fear.

A mirror-ledger sits open on the table, pages torn where influence was conserved. You must decide how to approach the scene without triggering an institutional alarm that could destroy your evidence.

You meet with the faction known as The New Men in their base of operations. They claim they are merely observers of the civilizational wager, but their eyes hold the ambition of those who wish to escape the cul-de-sac. You must decide whether to trust their testimony regarding the Mediator's final hours.
